html:
Jithin Thilakan joined the Erich Thienhaus Institute (ETI) at the Detmold University of Music in September 2019 as an early stage researcher (ESR) in VRACE, “Virtual Reality Audio for Cyber Environments,” an EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Innovative Training Network whose 15 ESRs across Europe cover virtual acoustics from sound generation to perception. His aim is to recreate a perceptually convincing spatial impression of ensemble playing in virtual reality: perception-oriented source signals and instrument directivities, how instruments blend, and what the room contributes.

Thilakan holds a master’s in applied physics from IIT (ISM) Dhanbad. He had no formal training in acoustics, but building a device to track vocal tract resonances with the Acoustics & Audio group at the Singapore University of Technology and Design drew him into the field. ETI is known for its bachelor’s and master’s Tonmeister programs and also offers a master’s and doctorate in music acoustics; it takes part in the international ACTOR project and has a 3D performance room, a wave field synthesis system and an anechoic chamber.

VRACE funded him fully, and ETI added six months to his 36-month contract to offset pandemic delays. First-year coursework is optional for students lacking an acoustics background, followed by a formal exposé; the thesis is a monograph, with no peer-reviewed papers required. Trained Tonmeister ears make ideal expert listeners, and English works fine at the institute. Planning to submit in autumn 2023, he values above all learning a systematic scientific approach to any problem.

Adapted into Chinese by Fanyu Meng from Jithin Thilakan’s first-person profile in Akustik Journal, published by the German Acoustical Society (DEGA).
